key_insight: AI agents could deepen inequality when people have unequal access to them or differ in the quality and number of agents they can use. This paper offers a conceptual framework for identifying these risks and a research agenda for addressing them.
problem_solved: Addresses the need to understand how unequal access to AI agents—and differences in their capabilities and availability—could create or amplify societal inequalities.
method: Develops a conceptual framework to identify potential sources of inequality involving AI agents.
Examines disparities in agent access, quality, and number.
Proposes a research agenda to investigate and help address these societal risks.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the paper highlights that equitable deployment requires attention not only to agent capabilities, but also to who can access and benefit from them. It provides a starting point for research into distributional consequences.
visual_elements: Three-axis diagram showing disparities in agent access, quality, and number.
Side-by-side illustrations of people supported by different numbers and capabilities of AI agents.
Conceptual flowchart linking agent disparities to potential societal inequalities.
Research-roadmap graphic connecting identified risks with questions for future study.
paper_authors: Matthew Sharp, Omer Bilgin, Iason Gabriel, Lewis Hammond
